title_en: Sun Changming v. Jiangsu Weite Group Co., Ltd. and Yancheng Economic Development Zone Xiangxin Rural Micro-credit Co., Ltd. — dispute over third-party enforcement objection
ruling_gist_en: 1. During execution, after a written objection raised by a third party to the subject matter of execution is dismissed, the third party shall, based on the relationship between its claimed rights and the original judgment or ruling, choose to safeguard its lawful rights and interests through either the trial supervision procedure or an enforcement objection lawsuit in accordance with law.

full_text_en:
Sun Changming v. Jiangsu Weite Group Co., Ltd. and Yancheng Economic Development Zone Xiangxin Rural Microcredit Co., Ltd. — dispute over execution objection by a third party

【Ruling Summary】

1. During the execution process, after a third party's written objection to the subject matter of execution is dismissed, the third party shall, based on the relationship between its claimed rights and the original judgment or ruling, lawfully choose to safeguard its legitimate rights and interests through either the trial supervision procedure or an action for execution objection.

2. The action for execution objection is a judicial remedy provided for the protection of a third party's rights. It is directed at the execution act itself, and its core lies in evaluating and determining whether the execution procedure should continue or be suspended, based on the precondition that the third party has a legitimate right sufficient to block the execution procedure. If the civil rights-obligation relationship to which the third party's rights claim pertains, or the subject matter to which its claims in the lawsuit relate, is identical to the civil rights-obligation relationship established by the original judgment or ruling or to the object of such relationship, and the subject matter of execution is the specific object of the rights-obligation relationship determined by the effective judgment or ruling serving as the basis for execution, then the case falls under the circumstances of "considering the original judgment or ruling to be erroneous" and shall be handled through the trial supervision procedure.

Civil Ruling of the Supreme People's Court
(2013) Min Ti Zi No. 207

Re-consideration Applicant (Plaintiff at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance): Sun Changming, male, Han ethnicity, born on May 19, 1959, residing in Yancheng City, Jiangsu Province.

Agent ad litem: Xu Yulin, lawyer of Jiangsu Yinguo Law Firm.

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance, Appellee at Second Instance): Jiangsu Weite Group Co., Ltd., domiciled at No. 28 Kaifang Avenue, Yancheng City, Jiangsu Province.

Legal Representative: Lu Yunlong, Chairman of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Xu Yang, General Manager of the Company.

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance, Appellee at Second Instance): Yancheng Economic Development Zone Xiangxin Rural Microcredit Co., Ltd., domiciled at Unit 102, First Floor, Huaxia Commercial Residential Building, Kaifang Avenue, Yancheng Economic Development Zone, Jiangsu Province.

Legal Representative: Zhou Chunxiang, Chairman of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Duan Junru, lawyer of Beijing Zhongzhou Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Zhou Sheng, lawyer of Beijing Zhongzhou Law Firm.

In the dispute over execution objection by a third party between the re-consideration applicant, Sun Changming, and the respondents, Jiangsu Weite Group Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Weite Company) and Yancheng Economic Development Zone Xiangxin Rural Microcredit Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Xiangxin Company), Sun Changming, dissatisfied with the civil judgment (2012) Su Min Zhong Zi No. 0160 rendered by the Jiangsu High People's Court on November 20, 2012, applied to this Court for re-consideration. This Court rendered the civil ruling (2013) Min Shen Zi No. 313 on June 21, 2013, approving the re-consideration and suspending the execution of the original judgment. This Court formed a collegial panel according to law and held a hearing of this case on November 14, 2013. Sun Changming and his agent ad litem Xu Yulin, the agent ad litem of Weite Company Xu Yang, and the agents ad litem of Xiangxin Company Duan Junru and Zhou Sheng appeared in court to participate in the proceedings. The case is now concluded.

The following facts were found at the first instance trial by the Yancheng Intermediate People's Court of Jiangsu Province (hereinafter referred to as Yancheng Intermediate Court):

On June 5, 2007, Weite Company borrowed money from the Yancheng Chengbei Sub-branch of China Construction Bank (hereinafter referred to as CCB Chengbei Sub-branch), and mortgaged the 5,110.24 square meters of the comprehensive building at No. 28 Kaifang Avenue, Yancheng City to CCB Chengbei Sub-branch. The said bank handled the cancellation of the mortgage registration for the above property on December 4, 2009. On the same day, Weite Company borrowed RMB 4 million from Xiangxin Company, and set a maximum amount mortgage on the 363.51 square meters of property at No. 28 Kaifang Avenue, Yancheng City, valued at RMB 5.3 million. The two parties signed the "Maximum Amount Mortgage Contract" and obtained the certificate of other rights. Location of the property: Ground floor and partial second floor (axes 1-5) of the comprehensive building at No. 28 Kaifang Avenue, Yancheng City. The registration date of the certificate of other rights was December 4, 2009.

On September 15, 1998, Weite Company signed a construction contract with Yancheng Wanghai Construction Engineering Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Wanghai Company), contracting the construction of the comprehensive building of Weite Company to Wanghai Company. Wanghai Company further subcontracted the project to Sun Changming, who was the actual constructor of the project. On October 20, 2009, Weite Company and Sun Changming signed an agreement, confirming that Weite Company owed Sun Changming RMB 4.05 million in construction costs, and agreed to offset part of the debt by transferring to Sun Changming two large rooms (axes 8-10) on the first-floor exhibition hall of the Weite Group comprehensive building (construction area: 103.85 square meters x 2) located at No. 28 Kaifang Avenue, Yancheng City, with a value of RMB 3,738,600, with the remaining balance to be settled separately. On October 26, 2010, the Tinghu District People's Court of Yancheng City, Jiangsu Province (hereinafter referred to as Tinghu Court) rendered the civil judgment (2010) Ting Shang Chu Zi No. 0476, confirming that the agreement signed between Sun Changming and Weite Company on October 20, 2009 was legally valid.

In the case of Xiangxin Company applying for execution against Weite Company, Weite Friction Materials Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Weite Materials Company), Yancheng Weite Brake Industry Technology Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Weite Brake Company), and Jiangsu Tianxingjian Construction Co., Ltd. in a loan contract dispute, Yancheng Intermediate Court enforced the above companies based on its civil judgments (2010) Yan Shang Chu Zi No. 0018, 0019, and 0020. When the court took compulsory execution measures against the mortgaged property registered under Weite Company, Sun Changming raised an execution objection. Yancheng Intermediate Court rendered the civil ruling (2011) Yan Zhi Yi Zi No. 0004 on April 25, 2011, holding that although Sun Changming had signed an agreement with Weite Company to transfer the property to satisfy a debt, the parties had not completed the registration of the property transfer. Sun Changming's claim that he had obtained ownership of the property in question could not be established, and therefore dismissed Sun Changming's execution objection. Dissatisfied, Sun Changming filed an action for execution objection by a third party with Yancheng Intermediate Court.

Sun Changming alleged in his lawsuit that: After the signing of the agreement on October 20, 2009, Weite Company delivered the property in question to Sun Changming. The loan and mortgage conduct between Xiangxin Company and Weite Company, Weite Materials Company, and Weite Brake Company occurred after Sun Changming lawfully obtained and actually took possession of the property in question. Weite Company had no right to mortgage the property in question to others. The licensed business scope of Xiangxin Company was to issue micro-loans to "agriculture, rural areas, and farmers." Xiangxin Company's issuance of a loan of RMB 15 million to Weite Company and its affiliated enterprises violated mandatory provisions of financial laws and regulations, rendering the principal loan contract void, and the guarantee contract as an ancillary contract also void. Xiangxin Company knew that Weite Company had already transferred the property in question to Sun Changming to offset construction costs, so the mortgage of the property in question by Weite Company and Xiangxin Company was an act of bad faith. After Weite Company transferred the property in question to Sun Changming, it failed to handle the transfer registration in a timely manner, which was caused by Weite Company's failure to perform its contractual obligations and violation of legal provisions. The legal consequences should be borne by Weite Company and the relevant entities. Therefore, he requested: 1. Confirmation that ownership of the two rooms (axes 8-10) on the first-floor exhibition hall of the Weite Group comprehensive building at No. 28 Kaifang Avenue, Tinghu District, Yancheng City (value RMB 3,738,600) belongs to Sun Changming; 2. Order Weite Company to continue performing the agreement signed by the parties; 3. Order Weite Company and Xiangxin Company to assist Sun Changming in handling the property transfer registration; 4. Suspend execution of the disputed property; 5. Costs of the action to be borne by Weite Company and Xiangxin Company.

Weite Company and Xiangxin Company responded that: 1. Sun Changming did not have standing as a plaintiff. 2. Before October 20, 2009, the property in question had been mortgaged to CCB Chengbei Sub-branch. Even if Weite Company owed construction costs to Sun Changming, its act of selling the mortgaged property damaged the interests of the mortgagee and should be void. 3. The judgments (2010) Yan Shang Chu Zi No. 0018, 0019, 0020 of Yancheng Intermediate Court all confirmed Xiangxin Company's lawful business operations. The loan agreement between Xiangxin Company and Weite Company was legally valid. Xiangxin Company's request for Weite Company to provide mortgage guarantee did not violate legal provisions. 4. Even if Weite Company owed construction costs to Sun Changming, since the property in question had been mortgaged to Xiangxin Company, Xiangxin Company's execution request should take precedence. Sun Changming's claims lacked factual and legal basis and should be dismissed.

The court of first instance held: I. Regarding whether Sun Changming was qualified as a plaintiff in this case: On October 20, 2009, Weite Company and Sun Changming signed an agreement transferring the property in question to Sun Changming to offset construction costs. Sun Changming had a direct interest in this case, and his lawsuit complied with the provisions of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Civil Procedure Law). Therefore, he had standing as a plaintiff. II. Regarding whether Sun Changming, as the actual constructor, had a priority right to be satisfied from the property in question: The time limit for a construction project contractor to exercise the priority right is six months, counted from the date of completion of the construction project or the date of completion agreed in the construction contract. This project was completed in October 1999. According to the above provisions, Sun Changming's priority right to be satisfied from the property in question had exceeded the protection period. III. Regarding whether Xiangxin Company's loan to Weite Company complied with legal provisions: This had already been determined by an effective judgment. Sun Changming's claim that Xiangxin Company's loan was illegal was not adopted. IV. Regarding whether Sun Changming had ownership of the property in question: Article 191, Paragraph 2 of the Property Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Property Law) provides that during the mortgage period, the mortgagor may not transfer the mortgaged property without the consent of the mortgagee, unless the transferee pays off the debts to extinguish the mortgage. On June 5, 2007, Weite Company mortgaged the 5,110.24 square meters of the comprehensive building involved to CCB Chengbei Sub-branch for a loan. The bank handled the cancellation of the mortgage registration on December 4, 2009. On the same day, Weite Company mortgaged the property in question to Xiangxin Company. On October 20, 2009, Weite Company and Sun Changming signed an agreement transferring the property in question to Sun Changming to offset construction costs. The above facts showed that a mortgage was established on the property in question. The time when Weite Company and Sun Changming signed the agreement fell within the mortgage period, violating the provisions of the Property Law. Sun Changming could not obtain ownership of the property in question. Although the Tinghu Court's judgment confirmed that the agreement signed between Sun Changming and Weite Company on October 20, 2009 was legally valid, since the parties failed to go through the property transfer registration, the ownership of the property in question did not change. Therefore, Sun Changming's claim to confirm ownership had no legal basis, and his request to order Weite Company to continue performing the contract to satisfy the debt with the property and to assist in the transfer registration was not supported. V. Regarding whether execution should be suspended: Suspension of execution belongs to the process of execution and will not be addressed in this case. After discussion by the judicial committee, the court rendered the civil judgment (2011) Yan Min Chu Zi No. 0036: dismissing all of Sun Changming's claims. The case acceptance fee of first instance, RMB 11,186, was borne by Sun Changming.

Dissatisfied with the judgment of first instance, Sun Changming appealed to the Jiangsu High People's Court.

Sun Changming appealed on the grounds that: 1. The agreement for the sale of the property in question between Sun Changming and Weite Company had been confirmed as valid by an effective court document. Therefore, it should be determined that Sun Changming had ownership of the property in question. 2. Sun Changming was the actual constructor of the property in question. During the process of demanding construction costs, he had been asserting the priority right to be satisfied for the construction costs against Weite Company. Based on this, Weite Company agreed to satisfy the debt with the property. This fact occurred before Xiangxin Company issued the loan. Xiangxin Company operated across regions, and the lending relationship between Weite Company and Xiangxin Company violated laws and regulations. The loan agreement was void. 3. According to Article 17 of the Supreme People's Court's Provisions on the Sealing, Distraint, and Freezing of Property in Civil Execution, although the property in question had not been registered for transfer, Sun Changming was not at fault. Therefore, the court should not take execution measures against the property in question. Therefore, he requested the court of second instance to amend the judgment and support his claims.

Weite Company responded that: 1. Sun Changming had not obtained ownership of the property in question. His claim to ownership of the property in question could not be established. 2. Xiangxin Company had no fault in obtaining the mortgage on the property in question. 3. Sun Changming did not have the priority right to be satisfied for construction costs. The construction contract relationship was between Weite Company and Wanghai Company, not Sun Changming personally. Moreover, Sun Changming's claim had exceeded the six-month period. Therefore, he requested the court of second instance to dismiss Sun Changming's appeal.

Xiangxin Company responded that: 1. The court judgment confirmed that the agreement between Sun Changming and Weite Company was valid, but it did not confirm that ownership of the property in question belonged to Sun Changming. 2. The issue of suspending execution should not be addressed in this case. 3. Sun Changming's claim for the priority right to be satisfied for construction costs had exceeded the exercise period. Therefore, he requested the court of second instance to dismiss the appeal and affirm the original judgment.

The facts found by the court of second instance were the same as those found by the court of first instance.

The court of second instance held that this case was an action for execution objection by a third party. Weite Company and Xiangxin Company signed a loan agreement, and Weite Company mortgaged the property in question. When Weite Company failed to repay the loan, Xiangxin Company applied to the court for execution of the property in question. Sun Changming, claiming that he had rights over the property in question, raised an execution objection. After his execution objection was dismissed by the court, Sun Changming filed this lawsuit, asserting that he had ownership of the property in question. Sun Changming and Weite Company had reached an agreement to satisfy the debt with the property in question. The agreement represented the true intent of the parties, did not violate prohibitive provisions of laws and regulations, and was confirmed as valid by an effective court judgment. However, the relationship between the parties remained one of creditor-debtor rights. Since a mortgage was established on the property in question, Sun Changming had been unable to complete the transfer of title. Currently, the title to the property in question remained registered under Weite Company's name, and Sun Changming had not obtained ownership. Therefore, this ground of appeal was not supported.

Regarding Sun Changming's ground of appeal that the loan agreement between Weite Company and Xiangxin Company was void, since the loan dispute between them had already been confirmed by an effective court judgment, Sun Changming's claim that the loan agreement was void had no legal basis.

Regarding Sun Changming's claim that he had a priority right to be satisfied from the property in question, he asserted that Weite Company owed him construction costs, thus the property in question was used to satisfy the debt. Although the Contract Law provides that a contractor may have priority in receiving payment from the discounted or auctioned price of the project in question, the law also sets a time limit for exercising the priority right. Sun Changming had not raised this claim within the statutory period. Therefore, Yancheng Intermediate Court's decision not to adopt such claim was not improper.

Regarding Sun Changming's claim that execution should be suspended: Since this case was an action for execution objection, the issue to be examined in this case was whether Sun Changming had rights over the subject matter of execution, i.e., the property in question. Issues related to the execution procedure could not be addressed in this case. Therefore, Yancheng Intermediate Court's decision not to address such claim was also not improper.

In summary, the court of second instance rendered the civil judgment (2012) Su Min Zhong Zi No. 0160: dismissing the appeal and affirming the original judgment. The case acceptance fee of second instance, RMB 11,186, was borne by Sun Changming.

Dissatisfied with the judgment of second instance, Sun Changming applied to this Court for re-consideration pursuant to Items 2 and 6 of Article 200 of the Civil Procedure Law, requesting the reversal of the judgment of second instance and the support of all his claims. His grounds were: 1. Weite Company had delivered the property in question to Sun Changming to offset construction costs. Sun Changming had been in possession and use of it until now. Therefore, he should have obtained ownership of the property in question. 2. Xiangxin Company's act of issuing the loan to Weite Company exceeded its business scope and constituted cross-region operation. As a professional loan company, Xiangxin Company was negligent in its review when issuing loans and establishing mortgages to Weite Company and its affiliated companies. It knew or should have known that the property in question belonged to Sun Changming, or at least should have known that the title to the property in question was in dispute. Nevertheless, it still completed the mortgage registration, demonstrating subjective fault. 3. The judgment of first instance in this case and the related judgments of Tinghu Court and Yancheng Intermediate Court exhibited discrepancies in adjudicating similar cases.

Weite Company responded that: 1. Weite Company's act of using the property in question to offset construction costs to Sun Changming and mortgaging it to Xiangxin Company both reflected the true intent of the parties. The fact that the offset occurred first and the mortgage was established later was a basic fact. 2. Xiangxin Company and Yancheng Intermediate Court were at fault during the execution process. 3. There were four related cases between Xiangxin Company and Weite Company, with total debts of RMB 18 million, but RMB 27.72 million had already been executed. Therefore, Xiangxin Company's claims had been fully satisfied. 4. Sun Changming was the actual constructor of the project in question. His legitimate rights and interests should be protected, and his ownership of the property in question should be confirmed.

Xiangxin Company responded that: 1. Sun Changming filed an action for execution objection by a third party, but his claims 2 and 3, as well as his assertion in the re-consideration application that the loan agreement and mortgage agreement between Xiangxin Company and Weite Company were void, were not within the scope of trial of this case. 2. Sun Changming did not have ownership of the property in question. 3. Sun Changming did not have a priority right to be satisfied from the property in question. Even if he were the actual constructor and had such a priority right, the right had exceeded the statutory exercise period. 4. Xiangxin Company had lawfully obtained the mortgage. Sun Changming's re-consideration application lacked factual and legal basis and should be dismissed.

This Court found upon re-consideration: On August 26, 2010, Yancheng Intermediate Court rendered civil judgments (2010) Yan Shang Chu Zi No. 0018, 0019, and 0020. All three judgments determined that if the debtor failed to repay the debt in accordance with the amount and time specified in the judgments, Xiangxin Company had the right to seek priority in payment from the proceeds of discounting, auction, or sale of the registered mortgaged property of Weite Company within the scope of such funds.

OPINION OF THE COURT

Article 227 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC provides that: "During the execution process, an outsider who raises a written objection to the subject matter of execution shall be reviewed by the people's court within fifteen days from the date of receipt of the written objection. If the reasons are established, the court shall rule to suspend the execution of such subject matter; if the reasons are not established, the court shall rule to dismiss the objection. If the outsider or a party is dissatisfied with the ruling and believes that the original judgment or ruling is erroneous, the matter shall be handled in accordance with the trial supervision procedure; if the matter is unrelated to the original judgment or ruling, an action may be instituted with the people's court within fifteen days from the date of service of the ruling." According to this provision, during the execution process, after a written objection raised by an outsider to the subject matter of execution has been dismissed by ruling, the outsider shall, based on the relationship between his or her claimed rights and the original judgment or ruling, choose in accordance with the law to protect his or her lawful rights and interests either through the trial supervision procedure or through an action for objection to execution. As a judicial remedy provided by law for the protection of an outsider's rights after the initiation of the execution procedure, an action for objection to execution is directed at the execution act itself. Its core lies in evaluating and determining whether the execution procedure should continue or be suspended, premised on whether the outsider has a legitimate right sufficient to block the execution procedure in relation to the subject matter of execution. However, if the civil rights-obligation relationship to which the outsider's claim points, or the subject matter to which his or her litigation claims point, is identical to the civil rights-obligation relationship determined by the original judgment or ruling, or to the object of such rights-obligation relationship, and if the subject matter of execution is the specific object of the rights-obligation relationship determined by the effective judgment serving as the basis for execution, then this falls under the circumstance of "believing that the original judgment or ruling is erroneous". In this case, after Sun Changming's written objection to the subject matter of execution was dismissed by ruling, he filed an action for objection to execution as an outsider with the court of first instance. The court of first instance and the court of second instance also conducted substantive trial of this case on such a cause of action. However, the enforcement measures taken by the Yancheng Intermediate People's Court against the property registered under the name of Weite Company, including the property involved in this case, which had already been subject to mortgage registration in favor of Xiangxin Company, were based on the relevant civil judgment that had already become legally effective of that court. The scope of property for which the effective civil judgment confirmed that Xiangxin Company enjoyed the mortgage right and had the right to be compensated with priority also included the property involved in this case. In his litigation reasons, Sun Changming also explicitly raised objections to the loan transaction between Xiangxin Company and Weite Company and to the validity of the mortgage right. His litigation claims were intended to deny the legality of the aforementioned effective civil judgment of the Yancheng Intermediate People's Court as the basis for execution. Under these circumstances, this case should fall under the circumstance provided for in Article 227 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC: "If the outsider or a party is dissatisfied with the ruling and believes that the original judgment or ruling is erroneous, the matter shall be handled in accordance with the trial supervision procedure." Sun Changming's resolution of the dispute in this case through an action for objection to execution as an outsider has no legal basis. In this litigation, the issue of whether the effective judgment contains errors cannot be resolved. The substantive trial of the relevant disputes by the court of first instance and the court of second instance in this case does not comply with the provisions of the law, and this Court corrects this error.

In summary, the judgments of the court of first instance and the court of second instance erroneously applied the law. Pursuant to Article 207, paragraph 1, Article 170, paragraph 1, item 2, and Article 227 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, this Court rules as follows:

1. The civil judgment (2012) Su Min Zhong Zi No. 0160 of the Jiangsu High People's Court and the civil judgment (2011) Yan Min Chu Zi No. 0036 of the Yancheng Intermediate People's Court of Jiangsu Province are hereby reversed;

2. The lawsuit filed by Sun Changming is dismissed.

This ruling is final.

Presiding Judge: Han Mei

Judge: Xin Zhengyu

Acting Judge: Si Wei

May 30, 2014

Clerk: Tang Qian
